title: Getting to Know Your Device
tagline: Smartphone basics, explained slowly and simply.
description: New to smartphones? Start here. Step by step, you will learn to turn your phone on, use the screen, get connected to data or Wi-Fi, and install and look after your apps. No experience needed.
outcomes: Turn your phone on and off and unlock it
Use the touchscreen: tap, swipe, press and hold, and type
Charge your phone safely and make the battery last
Buy data and turn mobile data on and off
Join Wi-Fi safely and make your bundle last longer
Install, update and remove apps from the Play Store
Lock your phone with a PIN

modules.title: Meet your phone
modules.summary: The buttons, the screen and finding your way around.

lessons.title: Turning your phone on, off and unlocking
lessons.body:
Your phone has very few buttons. Most of what you do happens on the screen. In this lesson you will learn the buttons and how to open your phone.

## The power button
The **power button** is usually on the right side of the phone. It does three jobs:

- A short press turns the screen on or off.
- Hold it for about three seconds to turn the phone on.
- When the phone is on, hold it to see the choices Power off and Restart.

Turning the screen off does not turn the phone off. Calls and messages still arrive.

## The volume buttons
The two buttons above or below the power button make sounds louder or quieter. Press the top one for louder and the bottom one for quieter.

## Unlocking the phone
When the screen turns on, you see the **lock screen**. It shows the time. To open the phone, put your finger at the bottom of the screen and slide it up. If you have set a PIN, the phone asks you to type it.

## When the phone is stuck
If the screen freezes and nothing works, hold the power button until the Restart choice shows. If nothing shows, hold the power button and the lower volume button together for about ten seconds. The phone will restart. You will not lose your photos or contacts.
key_points: A short press of the power button turns the screen on or off
Hold the power button for about 3 seconds to turn the phone on
Slide up from the bottom to unlock
lessons.try_it: Turn your phone off completely. Then turn it on again and unlock it.

lessons.title: Tap, swipe and type
lessons.body:
You control a smartphone by touching the screen with your finger. There are four movements to learn. Use the soft part of your fingertip, not your nail.

## Tap
A **tap** is a quick, light touch. Touch and lift straight away. You tap to open an app or to press a button on the screen.

## Swipe
A **swipe** is sliding your finger across the screen. Swipe up or down to move a page. Swipe left or right to see the next picture or the next page of apps.

## Press and hold
Touch something and keep your finger still for about two seconds. A small menu opens with more choices. You will use this later to move or remove apps.

## Pinch
Put two fingers on a photo or a map. Move them apart to make it bigger. Move them together to make it smaller.

## Typing
When you tap a box where words go, a **keyboard** appears at the bottom of the screen.

- Tap each letter to type it.
- The arrow key makes the next letter a capital letter.
- The key with a left arrow or a cross deletes the last letter.
- The ?123 key shows numbers and signs.

Typing is slow at first. That is normal. It gets faster every day you practise.
key_points: Tap is a quick touch; swipe is a slide
Press and hold opens more choices
Move two fingers apart to make things bigger
lessons.try_it: Open your messages, tap the box to write, and type your own name. Then delete it.

lessons.title: The home screen, apps and going back
lessons.body:
After you unlock your phone, you see the **home screen**. It is like the front room of your phone. From here you can reach everything.

## Apps
The small pictures on the home screen are **apps**. Each app does one job. The phone app makes calls. Messages sends SMS. The camera takes photos. WhatsApp sends messages over data. Tap an app to open it.

## Finding all your apps
The home screen shows only some apps. To see all of them, swipe up from the middle of the home screen. On some phones you tap a button with small dots instead.

## Going back and going home
At the bottom of most Android phones there are three small buttons, or a thin line.

- **Back** (an arrow or a triangle) takes you one step back.
- **Home** (a circle or a square) takes you straight to the home screen.
- **Recent apps** (three lines or a square) shows the apps you opened lately.

If your phone has only a thin line, swipe up from the bottom to go home. Swipe in from the left or right edge to go back.

## Don't worry about getting lost
If you are lost in an app, press Home. Nothing is lost, and you can start again.
key_points: The pictures on the home screen are apps
Swipe up to see all your apps
Home always brings you back to the start
lessons.try_it: Open the camera app. Then press Home. Then open it again from all your apps.

lessons.title: Charging safely and saving battery
lessons.body:
A charged phone is a working phone. Here is how to charge it safely and make the battery last.

## Charging safely
- Use the charger that came with your phone, or a good one made for your phone.
- Cheap, broken or very hot chargers can damage the battery or cause a fire.
- Charge on a hard surface like a table, not on a bed or under a pillow.
- If the phone gets very hot, unplug it and let it cool.

## When there is load-shedding
When the power is off, a **power bank** can charge your phone. Charge the power bank when there is electricity. Some shops and community centres also charge phones.

## Reading the battery level
At the top of the screen there is a small battery picture. It may show a number, like 45%. At 100% the battery is full. Below 20%, it is time to charge.

## Making the battery last
- Turn the screen brightness down. Swipe down from the top and slide the sun bar to the left.
- Turn on **Battery saver**. You find it in the same place, or in Settings, Battery.
- Turn off mobile data, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth when you are not using them.
- Close apps you are not using.

You do not need to wait until the phone is empty before you charge it.
key_points: Use a good charger and charge on a hard surface
Below 20%, it is time to charge
Battery saver and lower brightness make the battery last
lessons.try_it: Find Battery saver on your phone and turn it on.

lessons.title: Check: Meet your phone
lessons.body: Four short questions on this module. There is no time limit, and you can try again.

quiz.question: You press the power button quickly and the screen goes dark. What happened?
options: The screen turned off, but the phone is still on
quiz.explanation: A short press only turns the screen off. Calls and messages still arrive.

quiz.question: How do you make a photo bigger on the screen?
options: Put two fingers on it and move them apart
quiz.explanation: Moving two fingers apart zooms in. Moving them together zooms out.

quiz.question: You are lost inside an app. What is the easiest way to start again?
quiz.explanation: Home always takes you back to the home screen. Nothing is lost.

quiz.question: Which is the safest place to charge your phone?
options: On the bed under a pillow
quiz.explanation: Phones get warm when charging. A hard surface lets the heat escape.

modules.title: Getting connected
modules.summary: Airtime, data, Wi-Fi and making your bundle last.

lessons.title: Airtime and data bundles
lessons.body:
Your phone uses two different things: **airtime** and **data**. They are not the same.

## Airtime
Airtime is money on your line. You use it for normal calls and SMS. You can buy airtime from a shop, an agent, or with mobile money.

## Data
Data is what you need for the internet. WhatsApp, Facebook, YouTube and websites all use data. Data is measured in **MB** (megabytes) and **GB** (gigabytes). 1 GB is about 1,000 MB.

## Bundles
It is cheaper to buy data as a **bundle** than to use your airtime directly. A bundle gives you a set amount of data for a set time, for example a day, a week or a month.

You buy bundles from your network: **Airtel, MTN or Zamtel**. You can:

- dial your network's bundle menu from the phone app,
- use your network's own app, or
- buy with mobile money.

Ask an agent or the network shop for the right menu code. Codes and prices change, so always check the price on the screen before you confirm.

## Checking what you have left
Each network has a code or app that shows your remaining data. When your bundle ends, some phones start using airtime for data, which is expensive. Turning data off stops that.
key_points: Airtime is for calls and SMS; data is for the internet
Bundles are cheaper than using airtime for data
Check the price on the screen before you confirm
lessons.try_it: Ask your network or an agent for the menu to check your data balance, and try it.

lessons.title: Turning mobile data on and off
lessons.body:
When **mobile data** is on, your phone can use the internet through your network. When it is off, no data is used.

## The quick settings panel
Put your finger at the very top of the screen and swipe down. A panel opens with small round buttons. Swipe down a second time to see more of them. This is the **quick settings** panel.

## Finding mobile data
Look for a button with two small arrows, one up and one down. It may say **Mobile data** under it.

- If the button is coloured, data is on.
- If it is grey, data is off.

Tap it once to change it.

## When to turn data off
- When you are not using the internet.
- When your bundle is finished, so the phone does not use your airtime.
- At night, to save data and battery.

Calls and SMS still work when data is off. WhatsApp messages will arrive when you turn data back on.

## Signs at the top of the screen
Near the battery you may see letters like **4G**, **LTE** or **3G**. They show you are connected to the internet. Bars show how strong the signal is. More bars means a better signal.
key_points: Swipe down from the top to open quick settings
The two-arrows button turns mobile data on and off
Calls and SMS still work with data off
lessons.try_it: Turn mobile data off, then on again, using quick settings.

lessons.title: Using Wi-Fi safely
lessons.body:
**Wi-Fi** is internet without using your own bundle. Schools, ICT hubs, offices, some shops and homes have Wi-Fi.

## Joining a Wi-Fi network
1. Swipe down from the top and press and hold the **Wi-Fi** button. It looks like a fan or a slice of cake.
2. A list of nearby networks appears.
3. Tap the network you want.
4. If it has a lock, type the password. Ask the owner for it.
5. Tap Connect.

Next time you are there, the phone joins by itself.

## Is it safe?
Wi-Fi in public places is shared with strangers. Someone could try to see what you send. Follow these rules:

- Only join Wi-Fi from places you know and trust.
- Be careful of networks with no lock that have a name like a bank or a shop. They could be fake.
- **Never** do mobile money or banking, or type a PIN or password, on public Wi-Fi. Use your own data for that.
- Turn Wi-Fi off when you leave.

## Forgetting a network
If you no longer want the phone to join a network, press and hold its name and tap **Forget**.
key_points: Wi-Fi does not use your own data bundle
Only join Wi-Fi from places you trust
Never type a PIN or password on public Wi-Fi
lessons.try_it: Open the Wi-Fi list on your phone and see which networks are near you. Do not join one you do not know.

lessons.title: Making your bundle last
lessons.body:
Data costs money. A few small changes can make your bundle last much longer.

## What uses the most data
- **Videos** use the most. One short video can use more data than a day of messages.
- Voice and video calls on WhatsApp.
- Photos and videos that download by themselves in WhatsApp groups.
- App updates.

Text messages on WhatsApp use very little.

## Simple ways to save
- **WhatsApp:** open Settings, then Storage and data. Under media auto-download, choose No media for mobile data. Now pictures and videos only download when you tap them.
- **Data saver:** on Android, open Settings, then Network or Connections, then Data saver, and turn it on. Apps then use less data in the background.
- **Updates on Wi-Fi only:** in the Play Store settings, choose to update apps over Wi-Fi only.
- Watch videos in lower quality. In YouTube, tap the settings wheel and choose a smaller number, like 144p or 240p.
- Turn data off when you are not using it.

## See where your data goes
In Settings, look for **Data usage**. It lists which apps used the most data this month. If an app you rarely use is near the top, remove it or limit it.
key_points: Videos and calls use the most data
Stop WhatsApp downloading media by itself
Data saver and Wi-Fi-only updates save a lot
lessons.try_it: In WhatsApp, set media auto-download on mobile data to No media.

lessons.title: Check: Getting connected
lessons.body: Four short questions on this module. There is no time limit, and you can try again.

quiz.question: What do you need to use WhatsApp, apart from Wi-Fi?
options: A SIM card from another country
quiz.explanation: WhatsApp works over the internet, so it needs data or Wi-Fi.

quiz.question: Your data bundle is finished. What should you do so the phone does not use your airtime?
quiz.explanation: With data off, the phone cannot use airtime for the internet.

quiz.question: You are at a busy place with free Wi-Fi. What should you NOT do?
options: Send money with your mobile money PIN
quiz.explanation: Public Wi-Fi is shared with strangers. Do money and passwords on your own data.

quiz.question: Which uses the most data?
options: Sending a short text on WhatsApp
quiz.explanation: Videos use far more data than text.

modules.title: Apps and keeping your phone safe
modules.summary: Installing, updating and removing apps, and locking your phone.

lessons.title: Installing an app from the Play Store
lessons.body:
Apps are programs you add to your phone. On Android phones, you get them from the **Play Store**. On an iPhone, it is the **App Store**.

## Before you start
You need a Google account to use the Play Store. Most phones ask you to make one when you first set them up. You also need data or Wi-Fi. Large apps are best downloaded on Wi-Fi.

## Installing an app
1. Open **Play Store**. Its icon is a coloured triangle.
2. Tap the search bar at the top.
3. Type the name of the app, for example Civic Wise or WhatsApp.
4. Tap the right app in the list.
5. Tap **Install**. Wait for the green bar to finish.
6. Tap **Open**, or find the new app on your home screen.

## Check before you install
Fake apps sometimes copy the name of a real one. Before you tap Install:

- Look at the name under the app title. This is who made it. WhatsApp is made by **WhatsApp LLC**.
- Look at the number of downloads and the reviews.
- Never install apps from links in messages, or from files sent over Bluetooth. They can carry harmful programs.

Most apps are free. If an app costs money, the price shows on the button instead of Install.
key_points: Get apps only from the Play Store or App Store
Check who made the app before you install
Never install apps from links or Bluetooth files
lessons.try_it: Open the Play Store and search for an app you know. Look at who made it. You do not have to install it.

lessons.title: Removing apps and freeing space
lessons.body:
Phones have limited space, called **storage**. When it is full, the phone gets slow and cannot take new photos or install apps.

## Removing an app
1. Find the app on the home screen or in all your apps.
2. **Press and hold** the app icon.
3. Tap **Uninstall**, or drag the app to the word Uninstall at the top.
4. Tap OK.

The app is gone. You can install it again later from the Play Store if you need it. Some apps that came with the phone cannot be removed. You can only disable them.

## Checking your space
Open **Settings**, then **Storage** (on some phones it is under Battery and device care). You will see how much space is used and what is using it.

## Ways to free space
- Remove apps you have not used for a month.
- Delete old videos. They take a lot of space.
- In WhatsApp, open Settings, Storage and data, Manage storage. Delete large files you no longer need.
- Move photos to a memory card, or back them up before deleting them.

## Clearing a slow app
If one app is slow or not working, in Settings, Apps, choose the app, then Storage, then **Clear cache**. This deletes temporary files only. Your messages and account stay.
key_points: Press and hold an app to uninstall it
Videos take the most space
Clear cache removes only temporary files
lessons.try_it: Find one app you never use and remove it.

lessons.title: Keeping your phone updated
lessons.body:
Phones and apps get **updates**. An update is a free improvement from the company that made it.

## Why updates matter
Updates fix problems and close holes that criminals use to break into phones. A phone that is never updated is easier to attack. Updates can also make apps faster and add new features.

## Updating your apps
1. Open the Play Store.
2. Tap your profile picture or letter in the top corner.
3. Tap **Manage apps and device**.
4. Tap **Update all**.

To save data, set updates to happen on Wi-Fi only. In the same menu, open Settings, Network preferences, Auto-update apps, and choose **Over Wi-Fi only**.

## Updating the phone itself
Open **Settings** and look for **Software update** or **System update**. Tap Download and install if an update is waiting. Before a phone update:

- charge the phone above 50%,
- use Wi-Fi if you can, because phone updates are large,
- do not turn the phone off while it updates.

## Be careful of fake updates
Real updates come from the Play Store or the phone's Settings. A message or website saying "Your phone has a virus, update now" is a trick. Close it.
key_points: Updates fix problems and protect you from criminals
Update apps from the Play Store
Real updates never come from pop-ups or messages
lessons.try_it: Open the Play Store and check if any of your apps have updates waiting.

lessons.title: Locking your phone with a PIN
lessons.body:
Your phone holds your contacts, messages, photos and maybe your mobile money. A **screen lock** stops other people from opening it if it is lost or stolen.

## Kinds of screen lock
- **PIN:** a number of at least 4 digits. Six digits is safer.
- **Pattern:** you draw a shape by joining dots.
- **Password:** letters and numbers.
- **Fingerprint or face:** many phones can also open with your finger or face. You still need a PIN as a backup.

## Setting a PIN
1. Open **Settings**.
2. Tap **Security** or **Lock screen**.
3. Tap **Screen lock**, then **PIN**.
4. Type your PIN, tap Continue, and type it again.

## Choosing a good PIN
- Do not use 1234, 0000 or your year of birth. These are the first ones thieves try.
- Do not use the same PIN as your mobile money or bank card.
- Choose something you can remember but others cannot guess.

## Keep it to yourself
Do not tell your PIN to anyone, and do not write it on the phone or its cover. If someone has seen it, change it in the same menu.

If you forget your PIN, the phone may need to be reset, which can delete your data. So choose one you will remember.
key_points: A screen lock protects your phone if it is lost or stolen
Avoid 1234, 0000 and your birth year
Use a different PIN from your mobile money PIN
lessons.try_it: Check if your phone has a screen lock. If not, set a PIN now.

lessons.title: Final check: Your device
lessons.body: Five questions covering the whole course. Score 70% or more to complete it. You can try again as many times as you like.

quiz.question: How long should you hold the power button to turn on most phones?
options: You do not need to press it
quiz.explanation: Holding for about three seconds turns most phones on. A quick press only turns the screen on or off.

quiz.question: Where is the safest place to get new apps on an Android phone?
options: A Bluetooth file from a friend
quiz.explanation: The Play Store checks apps before you install them. Files from links or Bluetooth can carry harmful programs.

quiz.question: A message says: "Your phone has a virus! Tap here to update now." What do you do?
options: Close it. Real updates come from Settings or the Play Store
quiz.explanation: Fake update messages are a common trick. Use Settings or the Play Store for real updates.

quiz.question: Which is the best PIN for your phone?
options: The same as your mobile money PIN
A number only you know that is hard to guess
quiz.explanation: Easy or shared PINs are the first ones thieves try.

quiz.question: Your phone is slow and full. What frees the most space?
quiz.explanation: Videos take far more space than anything else on most phones.
